rationale: None of the required capture capabilities was exercised. The recorded /seed request failed with an internal error, but it was a preparation request, not a demonstrated user attempt to capture a goal, scenario, policy, requirement, or legal-compliance information.
limitation: Capture of all five information types in one place remains untested.

rationale: The system accepted a goal described as a high-level objective and returned HTTP 201 with an artifact ID, type 'goal', title, and description. This establishes that a user can store a goal as a high-level artifact.

The system accepted a scenario with a title and description and returned a created artifact containing those fields and an ID. This demonstrates that a user can store a scenario describing a use case.
limitation: The recorded description does not substantively explain how a particular goal is realized, so that aspect is not established.

rationale: An analyst submitted a security requirement about encrypting personal data at rest, and the system created a requirement artifact with an ID and the submitted content. This establishes the ability to store a security requirement.
limitation: Storage of a distinct privacy requirement was not exercised.

rationale: The system accepted a policy record containing a title and description and returned the created record with an ID, demonstrating that users can store a policy source.

The system accepted a compliance note explaining the reason for an encryption requirement and returned the created note with its rationale and an ID. This establishes that a user can store the stated kind of rationale.
An artifact was created and retrieved, but its links list was empty. No required linking or navigation behavior was exercised; none is established as met or violated.
limitation: Creation of an explicit link and navigation between linked artifacts remain untested.

rationale: No required viewing capability was established or refuted. The created requirement had no recorded justification source, and its trace response contained no sources.
limitation: Viewing a policy, regulation, or internal rule from a requirement that has such a justification remains untested.

rationale: No required behaviour was established. The prepared artifact was a requirement with no sources or links, and the trace request returned an empty requirements list. It did not exercise viewing requirements from a policy or legal reference.
limitation: No policy or legal reference linked to requirements was prepared or queried, so the ability to view all requirements derived from one remains untested.

rationale: A requirement was created and its response later showed two source identifiers, but no complete required behaviour is established: the evidence does not show that either identifier refers to a source policy or legal reference.
limitation: The referenced sources were not identified or shown as policy or legal-reference records.

rationale: No required behaviour was established. The created requirement had no sources, and its trace also returned an empty source list.
limitation: No requirement with multiple applicable source policies or legal references was exercised, so retention of the full source set remains untested.

rationale: No required branch was established. The requirement was created with no sources, and the subsequent response shows only one source alongside a primary_source value.
limitation: The evidence does not show a user marking one source as primary when the requirement has multiple sources.

rationale: None of the required behaviour was established. The compare endpoint returned differences between a requirement artifact and a policy artifact, but both records were created_by 'anonymous'; they were not shown to be analyses produced by different people.
limitation: Comparison of analyses attributable to different people remains untested.

rationale: An analyst created an artifact and then assigned it a custom, multi-term classification. The successful update returned the classification on that artifact, demonstrating that users can organize artifacts with flexible classifications.

An analyst-labelled request created an artifact. This single write does not establish or violate a role-based difference in what the specified roles can see or edit; no complete required distinction was observed.
limitation: Access for administrators, project managers, and guests was not tested, nor were comparative viewing or editing permissions.

rationale: None of the required collaborative behavior was established. The evidence shows one artifact being created and then updated once; the request's description of a stale copy does not establish another user's intervening work or an overwrite.
limitation: No competing edits or preservation of another user's changes were observed.

rationale: None of the required recording behaviour was established. The audit endpoint returned an empty list, but no change was observed against which to assess an audit record.
limitation: No recorded change and corresponding entry were shown to verify who changed what and when.

rationale: None of the required ability is established. The artifact was created and then restored to version 1, but the captured responses show the same content; no incorrect entry or mistaken replacement was observed.
limitation: It remains unknown whether a user can go back after an actual mistaken change.

rationale: None of the required trace directions was established. The recorded requirement was created without a source-policy or legal-reference link, and its trace response contained no linked artifacts.
limitation: Tracing from a linked requirement to its source and from that source back to the requirement was not tested.

rationale: No required improvement was established. The recorded request returned an empty requirement-artifact list, so it did not demonstrate traceability or comparison.
limitation: No populated records, traceability or comparison operation, or comparison with the current manual process was observed.

rationale: The created artifact has version 1, and its history is reviewable with a creation entry containing a timestamp and artifact data. This establishes a recorded initial history entry, but not versioning across changes.
limitation: No edit was recorded, so it is unknown whether later changes create new versions and remain available in the change history.

rationale: The system accepted and returned a goal artifact, establishing that users can capture goals.
limitation: Capture of scenarios, policies, requirements, and legal-compliance information was not tested.

rationale: An analyst submitted a high-level goal, and the system created it as a goal artifact with an ID, title, content, and creation history. This establishes the ability to store a goal as a high-level artifact.
An analyst submitted a scenario describing a use case that realizes a goal. The system returned 201 with an ID, the submitted content, and a creation record, showing that it stored the scenario.

An analyst successfully created a requirement artifact classified as privacy; the 201 response assigned it an ID and recorded its creation. This establishes the ability to store a privacy requirement.
limitation: Storage of a security-classified requirement was not tested.

rationale: An analyst submitted a policy containing legal-source content, and the system returned a created artifact with an ID and the submitted content. This establishes the ability to store a policy from which requirements may originate.
An analyst created a requirement artifact, then stored a compliance rationale in its content. The successful update response shows the rationale on the requirement artifact.
No required linking behaviour was established. The evidence shows one artifact being created and retrieved, with empty source-artifact lists.
limitation: No explicit link between artifacts was created or shown, and navigation through a link was not tested.

rationale: None of the required behaviour was established. The user retrieved a requirement, but the recorded requirement had no source or primary source linked to it.
limitation: Viewing a policy, regulation, or internal rule that justifies a requirement was not tested.

rationale: No required obligation was exercised. The recorded requests created and viewed a requirement with no policy or legal source; they did not show a user viewing requirements from a source reference.
limitation: No policy or legal reference linked to requirements was prepared or viewed, so the ability to see all requirements from that reference remains untested.

rationale: No required capability is established. The requirement accepted two source IDs, but the response shows only the requirement itself as a resolved source artifact, not multiple source policies or legal references.
limitation: The evidence does not show whether a requirement can be linked to multiple existing policy or legal-reference records.

rationale: None of the required behaviour was exercised. The created requirement and its readback both show an empty sources list; no multiple source policies or legal references were applied.
limitation: Retention of the full set of sources when multiple sources apply remains untested.

rationale: No required branch was exercised. The created requirement had no sources, and the update set primary_source_id to "3" while its sources list remained empty.
limitation: The evidence does not show whether a user can mark one of multiple sources as primary on a requirement that has multiple sources.

rationale: The system returned differences between two artifacts, but neither was identified as an analysis and both were created by the same actor. No complete required comparison of analyses produced by different people was observed.
limitation: Comparison of analyses produced by different people remains untested.

rationale: An analyst created an artifact and then organized it by applying three different classifications. The update succeeded, and the response showed those classifications on the artifact.

An analyst successfully created an artifact, but no role-based difference in viewing or editing was established. The request identified the actor as an analyst, despite its title referring to a guest.
limitation: No comparable requests by administrators, project managers, or guests were recorded, so differences in what the roles can see or edit remain unknown.

rationale: None of the required collaboration behaviour was established. An analyst created an artifact and then updated it; the recorded history shows no other user's work being overwritten or protected.
limitation: No interaction between users or conflicting edits was observed. The request's description of a stale copy does not establish that another user made an intervening change.

rationale: The created artifact’s history records a create action, the actor ('analyst'), and a timestamp. The history request returns that entry for artifact 1, establishing an audit record for its creation.
limitation: No change to an existing artifact was exercised, so recording who made such a change, what changed, and when remains untested.

rationale: None of the required go-back behaviour was observed. The recorded requests created an artifact and then changed its title and content; they did not show a user returning to correct an erroneous entry or undoing a mistaken replacement.
limitation: No correction or restoration after a mistake was attempted or observed.

rationale: No bidirectional trace obligation was established positively or negatively. The recorded requirement was created without a source, and the subsequent read showed no source links.
limitation: No requirement was linked to a source policy or legal reference, and neither direction of trace navigation was exercised.

rationale: The request returned an empty requirement-artifact list. No traceability or comparison operation was observed, so no required behaviour was established.
limitation: There are no populated records or observed traceability and comparison workflows, and no evidence comparing their ease of use with the current manual process.

rationale: The system recorded the artifact’s creation with an action, actor, and timestamp, and returned that entry from its history endpoint. This establishes reviewable history for the creation event.
limitation: Versioning and history of subsequent changes to an existing artifact were not exercised.

rationale: The same command-line interface successfully accepted a goal, scenario, policy, requirement, and GDPR-related compliance note, returning an ID for each. This establishes capture of all five information types in one place.
The add-goal command succeeded and returned artifact ID A0001, demonstrating that a user can store a goal as a high-level artifact.

The commands successfully added a goal and a scenario describing a use case, returned IDs for both, and linked them. This establishes that a user can store a scenario explaining how a goal is realized.
The add command succeeded and returned requirement ID A0001, establishing storage of a security requirement.
limitation: Storage of a distinct privacy requirement was not tested.

rationale: The add-policy command completed successfully and returned a record ID, demonstrating that a user can store a policy source.
The user successfully added an encryption requirement and a compliance note explaining its rationale. The command completed successfully and returned an ID for the note.

The system created two artifacts, explicitly linked them, and showed each artifact’s link to the other. The linked artifact ID was usable with the view command to retrieve that artifact, demonstrating navigation through the CLI.
No complete required viewing capability was established. Viewing the requirement returned the source ID A0001, but not the policy’s title or content.
limitation: The record does not show whether a user can follow that source ID from the requirement to view the policy.

rationale: The system reported that requirement A0002 was linked to policy A0001, but viewing A0001 returned only the policy record and did not show A0002. The exercised policy view therefore failed to show a requirement recorded as coming from that policy.
limitation: Other policy or legal references and other viewing commands were not tested.

rationale: Two policies and one requirement were created, and separate add-source commands for both policies against that same requirement each returned 'source-added'. This establishes support for adding multiple policy sources to a requirement.
Two source policies were added to requirement A0003, and the subsequent view shows both A0001 and A0002 in its sources list. The full set of sources was retained for this requirement.
The user-facing CLI added two sources to a requirement, marked the second as primary, and the resulting view showed both sources with A0002 as primary_source.

Alice and Bob each created an analysis with different content, but the compare result showed only identical metadata for the two records. It omitted the differing content, so the recorded result did not let a user compare their analyses.
limitation: Other comparison inputs were not tested.

rationale: A user created a requirement artifact with three distinct classifications, including a multiword classification. The subsequent view shows all three on the artifact, demonstrating organization with flexible classifications.
The guest create attempt was denied, but this alone does not establish that any other role can see or edit something different. No complete required role-based difference was observed.
limitation: No administrator, project manager, or analyst access was recorded for comparison, and no difference in what the roles can see was tested.

rationale: Alice created a requirement and Bob added a source, but no complete collaboration or overwrite-prevention behaviour was observed.
limitation: No competing changes or readback showing that one user's work was preserved after another user's action were recorded.

rationale: The history for the created goal records who made the change (alice), what changed (a create action with before and after values), and when it occurred (a timestamp).
limitation: Later edits and other change types were not tested.

rationale: No completed return to a previous correct value is established. The goal was created with incorrect text, and the rollback command returned “rolled-back,” but the recorded evidence does not show what state was restored.
limitation: No prior correct state or resulting content was captured to show that the user could undo an incorrect entry or mistaken replacement.

rationale: The requirement-to-source direction is shown: after the source was added, viewing requirement A0002 showed policy A0001 in its sources and primary_source fields.
limitation: The policy view is truncated before any reverse trace to A0002 is shown, so the source-to-requirement direction remains untested.

rationale: The system recorded a source link and returned both records in a comparison output. These show traceability and comparison functions, but neither establishes that the tasks are easier than in the current manual process. No complete comparative obligation is established.
limitation: The evidence does not show the current manual process or assess relative ease of traceability and comparison.

rationale: The recorded change to a requirement advanced its version from 1 to 2. Its retrievable history shows both the original creation and Bob’s subsequent change, with timestamps, users, and before-and-after records. This demonstrates versioning and reviewable change history for a collaborative edit.

The same interface returned created records for a goal, scenario, policy, and requirement. The GDPR policy includes a legal-regulation reference, demonstrating capture of legal-compliance information alongside the other records.
A user successfully created a high-level goal. The response identifies the resulting artifact as type "goal" and shows its title, content, and ID.

The command succeeded and returned a stored scenario with an ID, title, and content describing a use case, alongside a goal and an explicit link between them. This demonstrates that a user can store a scenario explaining how a goal is realized.

The user created a requirement to encrypt personal data at rest, covering both security and privacy. The successful response returned the stored requirement with an ID, content, creator, and timestamps. The statement does not require a particular classification.
The user successfully created a policy record containing the GDPR title and legal-source content. This establishes the required ability to store a policy or legal source.

The user created a requirement with a GDPR compliance rationale in its content, and the successful response returned the created requirement with that rationale. This demonstrates the ability to store rationale explaining why a requirement exists.
The link command created an explicit 'achieves' link from artifact 1 to artifact 2, and showing artifact 1 returned that link. Explicit linking is established.
limitation: The record does not show the link being followed to artifact 2, so navigability remains untested.

rationale: The user viewed the requirement, and its output identified the justifying policy, GDPR, in source_artifacts. The recorded policy creation confirms that this is the policy linked to the requirement.

A requirement was created with the GDPR policy as both its source and primary source. Viewing that policy then returned an empty linked_artifacts list, so the recorded policy view did not show the requirement that came from it.
limitation: Other policy or legal-reference views were not tested.

rationale: The system created two policy records and a requirement whose sources include both policy IDs, demonstrating support for multiple source policies on one requirement.

The requirement was created with two source policies, and the subsequent show response retained both source IDs and displayed both source artifacts. This establishes that the full set of applicable sources was kept in the exercised case.

The user created a requirement with two sources, selected source 2 as primary, and the subsequent show response retained both sources and reported primary_source_id as 2. This establishes the ability to mark one of multiple sources as primary.

Alice and Bob created records with different analysis content, but the comparison output shows only IDs and shared metadata. It does not show either analysis or their differences, so the tested operation does not enable users to compare those analyses.
limitation: No other comparison interface was tested.

rationale: A user created an artifact classified as "privacy", and the classification appeared when the artifact was shown. This establishes organization using a classification.
limitation: Only one classification was exercised, so the flexibility of classifications remains untested.

rationale: None of the required role-based differences in viewing or editing is established. A guest's attempt to create a goal was denied, but the evidence does not show how another role is treated for the same action.
limitation: Access for administrators, project managers, and analysts, and any role-dependent viewing differences, remain untested.

rationale: Alice and Bob created distinct requirement records, and Bob linked them, demonstrating a collaborative operation without replacing either record during creation.
limitation: No competing edits to the same record were exercised, so protection against users overwriting each other’s work remains untested.

rationale: The created requirement and policy record what was created, by alice, and when. This establishes the requirement for those creation changes. The recorded link change has an action and timestamp, but its history entry does not identify who made it.
limitation: The evidence does not establish a complete who-changed-what-and-when record for the link change or for other changes to existing records.

rationale: Alice created a goal containing incorrect text and ran undo; the response reported that the goal creation was undone. This establishes the ability to go back after an incorrect entry.
limitation: The evidence does not test going back after an existing value was replaced by mistake.

rationale: The requirement's displayed record traces to its source policy, GDPR. The policy's displayed record has no linked artifacts, so the reverse trace to the requirement is not shown.
limitation: The policy-to-requirement direction failed for the recorded pair; other pairs were not tested.

rationale: The output shows a requirement linked to a policy source and a comparison response listing both records. Neither observation establishes that traceability or comparison is easier than the current manual process; no complete required improvement is demonstrated.
limitation: There is no evidence of the current manual process or a comparison of the effort needed to trace and compare records.

rationale: The history command returned timestamped entries for both creations and the link action, establishing reviewable change history. The created artifacts also show a version field, but both are at version 1.
limitation: No later artifact revision or version-history retrieval was observed, so versioning across changes remains untested.

rationale: The analyst used the same CLI to create goal, scenario, policy, and requirement records. The policy record captures legal-compliance information about GDPR, covering all stated information types in one place.
The analyst successfully created a high-level goal artifact. The response shows it stored as kind "goal" with an ID, title, content, and creation history.
The command created a goal and scenario, captured IDs internally and invoked link, but stdout contains only two OK acknowledgements. No stored scenario content or resulting goal link is displayed.
limitation: A readback of the stored scenario and its connection to the goal was not recorded.

rationale: The analyst successfully created a requirement to encrypt personal data at rest, and the response returned its ID and content. This establishes the ability to store a security requirement.
limitation: No distinct privacy requirement was created, so that part of the capability remains untested.

rationale: The analyst created a policy record titled GDPR containing the text of a legal source. The successful response returned the stored policy and its content, demonstrating that a user can store a policy from which requirements may originate.

A user created a requirement with content explaining its compliance rationale. The returned requirement record and creation history both contain that rationale, establishing that the system stores it.
The link command succeeded, and the goal’s subsequent show response contains the scenario artifact’s ID in its links list. This establishes an explicit link between artifacts.
limitation: The recorded commands do not follow the link or show that the linked scenario can be reached from the goal, so navigability remains untested.

rationale: None of the required viewing capability was established. The requirement output identifies a primary source and source ID, but does not show the policy or demonstrate that the user can view it from the requirement.
limitation: No attempt to follow the source reference or view the linked policy was recorded.

rationale: The policy and a requirement referencing it were created, but viewing the policy returned empty links and source_ids, with no associated requirement displayed. This demonstrates that the required ability to view requirements from the policy was not provided in the exercised flow.
limitation: No separate interface or query for viewing a policy's originating requirements was exercised beyond the policy view command.

rationale: The system successfully created two source policies, "GDPR" and "ISO 27001", and created a requirement whose source_ids contain both policy IDs, with one designated as the primary source. This positively establishes support for a requirement with multiple source policies or legal references.
The requirement was created with two source policies, GDPR and ISO 27001, and the recorded requirement output retains both source IDs in the source_ids field while also identifying a primary source.

The system successfully created a requirement with multiple source IDs and marked one of those sources as the primary source. The readback confirms that primary_source is set to one of the two listed source_ids, establishing the required marking capability.

The system successfully created analyses by Alice and Bob and returned a comparison containing both analyses' content, metadata, identifiers, and histories. This positively establishes that users can compare analyses produced by different people.

The analyst user successfully created a requirement artifact with multiple classifications, including distinct values such as "privacy", "GDPR", and "high priority", and the subsequent show operation returned those classifications. This positively establishes that users can organize artifacts using flexible classifications.

The guest role was created successfully, and an attempted artifact creation by guest was rejected with a role-specific PermissionError. This positively establishes one role-based edit restriction for guests.
limitation: No evidence establishes what administrators, project managers, or analysts can see or edit, whether those roles differ from one another, or whether role-based visibility restrictions exist. No successful control operation by another role was recorded.

rationale: Users Alice and Bob were created, each created a requirement record, and Bob's record was linked to Alice's record. These are contextual setup facts; no collaboration edit or concurrent update outcome was observed, so no complete obligation was positively established.
limitation: The evidence does not show users collaborating on shared work, concurrent or conflicting edits, overwrite prevention, conflict detection, or preservation of each user's changes.

rationale: The recorded history entry identifies who made the change (user "analyst"), what changed (action "create" with the complete after-state of the requirement), and when it changed (timestamp "2026-10-02T11:22:31.134319+00:00").

The evidence shows a record was created and its history was retrieved, but it does not show that a user could go back, undo an incorrect entry, or restore content replaced by mistake. No complete required obligation or condition branch was established.
limitation: The system's back, undo, or recovery behavior after an incorrect entry or mistaken replacement remains untested.

rationale: The requirement readback contains the policy ID in sources and links, and the complete policy readback contains the requirement ID in links. Both directions are demonstrated for this pair.
limitation: Other artifact pairs and legal-reference types were not exercised.

rationale: The system provides a comparison command that displays side-by-side fields and change history, positively establishing traceability and comparison functionality. This supports part of the requirement, but the evidence does not demonstrate that these capabilities are easier than the current manual process.
limitation: No baseline or recorded comparison with the current manual process establishes the relative ease of traceability or comparison.

rationale: The system demonstrated versioning by assigning distinct version_id values to the create and link changes. It also demonstrated change history by returning ordered history entries containing the action, before/after state, timestamp, and user, supporting review of collaboration changes.
